architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added hostname safety validation to prevent PostgreSQL data sync connections to unsafe addresses including wildcards (0.0.0.0, ::), loopback, link-local, multicast, and reserved IPs
architecture_decisions.rationale: Wildcard addresses pose security risks as they could allow connections to unintended interfaces or expose internal services. The validation ensures data sync connections are made to specific, non-wildcard endpoints, preventing potential security vulnerabilities in data synchronization
alternatives_considered: Only checking for wildcard addresses (0.0.0.0 and ::) specifically
Adding validation at the UI/API layer instead of the data sync connection layer
Using a simpler regex-based approach instead of IP address resolution and classification

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Created a reusable utility function `is_hostname_safe()` in core utils that performs comprehensive IP address safety checks
architecture_decisions.rationale: Placing the validation logic in a core utility function makes it reusable across the codebase and follows the DRY principle. The function uses Python's built-in `ipaddress` module for proper IP address parsing and classification, ensuring accurate detection of unsafe address types
alternatives_considered: Implementing validation directly in the PostgreSQL data sync type class
Creating a separate validation module specific to data sync

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added validation at connection time with a clear error message when unsafe hostnames are detected
architecture_decisions.rationale: By validating at the point of connection establishment, we ensure security checks are always performed. The error message 'It's not allowed to connect to this hostname.' provides immediate feedback while maintaining security by not revealing too much detail about why the hostname is unsafe
alternatives_considered: Providing more detailed error messages explaining exactly which type of unsafe address was detected
Validating during configuration save instead of connection time
Using different exception types for different unsafe address categories

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added comprehensive test coverage for the new `is_hostname_safe()` function and updated existing `get_all_ips()` tests
architecture_decisions.rationale: Tests verify the function correctly identifies safe vs. unsafe addresses across different IP categories (wildcard, loopback, link-local, multicast, reserved). The tests use the `# noqa: S104` comment to suppress security linter warnings for test cases that intentionally use wildcard addresses
alternatives_considered: Only testing the specific wildcard addresses mentioned in the requirements
Mocking DNS resolution instead of testing with actual IP strings
Adding integration tests with actual PostgreSQL connections

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added detailed docstring for `is_hostname_safe()` function explaining what constitutes unsafe addresses
architecture_decisions.rationale: Clear documentation helps other developers understand the security rationale and ensures consistent usage. The docstring explicitly lists all unsafe address categories (wildcard, loopback, link-local, multicast, reserved) that the function checks for
alternatives_considered: Adding comments inline in the function body
Creating separate documentation in a security guide
Relying on function name and parameter names alone

tickets.title: Implement hostname safety validation for PostgreSQL data sync
tickets.description: Add security validation to prevent PostgreSQL data sync connections to unsafe IP addresses including wildcards, loopback, and other restricted addresses

implementation_summary:
The implementation adds security validation to prevent PostgreSQL data sync connections to unsafe IP addresses, with a primary focus on wildcard addresses (0.0.0.0 and ::) as requested. The solution was implemented by creating a new utility function `is_hostname_safe()` in the core utils module that performs comprehensive IP address safety checks. This function resolves hostnames to IP addresses using the existing `get_all_ips()` function, then uses Python's `ipaddress` module to classify each IP and check for unsafe categories including wildcard, loopback, link-local, multicast, and reserved addresses.

The validation is integrated into the PostgreSQL data sync connection establishment process in `postgresql_data_sync_type.py`, where it checks the hostname before attempting to establish a connection. If an unsafe hostname is detected, a `SyncError` is raised with a clear error message. This approach ensures validation happens at the right time (connection establishment) and provides immediate feedback to users.

The implementation maintains backward compatibility by only adding validation without changing existing behavior for safe addresses. Comprehensive tests were added to verify the validation works correctly for various IP address types, and a changelog entry was created to document the security enhancement. The solution follows the existing codebase patterns by placing reusable utilities in core modules and integrating validation into the appropriate business logic layer.
